page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Below the last line, at the right, one catchword. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: sitæ, quarum acropolis sive arx Cadmea à Cadmo Phœnice Agenoris filio, qui primus literarum usum in Græciam intulisse dicitur, condita nomen idem apud posteros retinuit. Urbs hæc perantiqua variis casibus jactata sub regibus, maximè sub filiis & nepotibus Oedipi. Regum ultimus Xanthus à Melantho Andropompi filio Athenienfi é posteris Nelei Pyliensis in monomachia occisus anno post excisam Trojam LVI, ante mortem Codri postremi Atheniensium regis Melantho nati LVII, & ante Heraclidarum reditum in Peloponnesum XXIV, locum dedit constituendæ libertati, ut tradit Pausanias.

Is enim sic ait : Τόδε [illegible, ~10 letters] πολιτεύσειν, μηδὲ ἀπ' ἀνδρὸς ἑνὸς ἡγεῖσθαι τὰ πάντα, ἀμείνων ἐφαίνετο τοῖς Θηβαίοις. Atque ab hoc tempore & urbs Thebana, & fortuna ejus magnum cepit incrementum. Sed an statim populo rerum summa permissa sit, an penes optimates reipublicæ potestas post regni finem fuerit, non est planum. Cum temporis autem progressu, cum Medi & Persæ jam rerum in Oriente potirentur, & Græcia maximè floreret, populum re-rum[?] arbitrium fuisse, satis constat.

page.notes: Greek opening words of the Pausanias quotation (first line) are not legible enough to copy letter by letter; left as illegible. Second Greek line is copied as read and may contain accent errors. The line break "re-" / "rum" in "populum rerum" is partly obscured by the gutter and marked [?]. Faint marks at the lower left margin (fragments such as "m", "piq rim") look like show-through or bleed from the facing page and are left out, as are the printed red/edge shadows. The catchword "Verùm" is taken as printed at the lower right.
